findings.F1: In falling-calm bars, 3-day excess returns rise across the scaled 7-day move. The largest falls (quintile 0) are followed by -1.79 % (t -1.63, 170 cases on 77 days), quintile 1 by -1.70 % (t -2.07, 74 days), and the largest rises (quintile 4) by +1.52 % (t 1.13, 35 days). That points to continuation, but only one of the five cells reaches |t| 2.
findings.F2: The graded slope of the 3-day excess return on the scaled move is positive in every grouping tried, and none clearly clears chance. In falling-calm it is 0.0104 for the 7-day move (t 1.57, 537 cases, 194 days) and 0.0119 for the 14-day move (t 1.99). Choppy markets give 0.0200 for the 14-day move (t 1.99), all bars 0.0061 (t 1.58), and outside the profile 0.0036 (t 0.81). This comes from about 50 slope cells across 3 lookbacks, 2 horizons and several regimes.
findings.F3: The falling-calm continuation is not stable over time. Short-direction 3-day excess returns after 7-day falls are +2.39 % in 2018 (t 1.93) and +1.85 % in 2019 (t 1.92), then -2.09 % in 2020 (t -1.33) and -1.15 % in 2021 (t -0.75). The 7-day slope by year changes sign too: 2018 +0.0165 (t 1.68), 2019 -0.0069, 2020 -0.0132, 2021 +0.0078.
findings.F4: Across coins in falling-calm, the 7-day slope is positive for all six (0.0000 to 0.0187) but no single coin reaches t 2 (highest 1.62 for ETH, 75 cases).
findings.F5: The book's gain rests on a few crash days. Its best 2 % of days (29 days) earn +4.55 % while the coins fall 7.88 %, and its worst 2 % lose 3.22 % while the coins rise 5.89 %. By window, only w7 (+0.11 %/day) and w14 (+0.27 %/day) have clearly positive means; 8 of 12 windows are negative.
findings.F6: Trades entered on the largest forecasts (top third of |entry forecast|) net +1.80 % with a 50 % win rate, against -0.21 % and -0.67 % for the lower two thirds (about 277 trades each). This is in line with a graded effect, but it is trade-level and dominated by the same crash days as F5.
findings.F7: Other angles show nothing beyond chance. The 1-day scaled move gives quintile |t| ≤ 0.96, weekdays give |t| ≤ 1.04, and the 7-day horizon slopes in falling-calm reach at most t 1.49.

no_ideas: Every pattern seen is a weak, same-sign version of the tested continuation (slopes with t at most 1.99 among about 50 cells looked at), it changes sign between years, and the book's gain comes from a handful of crash days, so nothing stands out enough from chance to support a new idea.
